data.architecture: Write path is layered: extension.mjs resolves the linked vault (config.json -> ResearchVault.open -> bind), controller.mjs acquires a `_Research/writer.lock` single-writer lock and drives session projection, and vault.mjs owns every filesystem write through an atomic temp-file+rename primitive (`_atomic`) guarded by per-path promise serialization. Notes are projected from native Pi session entries; message JSON records are immutable and content-hashed. Structured sidecars (metadata.json, manifest.json, packet/report JSON) carry provenance; Markdown notes are the human-facing surface. The Obsidian companion (obsidian/main.js from plugin.cjs + presentation.cjs + visual.cjs + styles.css) is installed into .obsidian/plugins/pi-research/ and handles live rendering and the request/result formatting check under _Research/presentation/.
data.report: # pi-discover vault writes, templating, and source grounding All anchors are `file:line` against the fetched source. `local://pi-discover-src/` = repo root. ## 1. Vault folder layout, files written, filename rules, frontmatter, write semantics ### Layout (from code; README storage diagram matches) ``` / Conversations// manifest.json vault.mjs:229,315,367 Conversation.md vault.mjs:338 (projected transcript) Messages/.json vault.mjs:308 (immutable record) Messages/.md vault.mjs:331 (projected) sessions/ vault.mjs:228 (mkdir) session.jsonl | sessions/*.jsonl vault.mjs:358-368 (setSessionFile) origin.json controller.mjs:220,239 (continue/fork metadata) draft.json controller.mjs:246,261,316 Reviews// packet.json review.mjs:120 session.jsonl review.mjs:122 report.json review.mjs:156 Review.md review.mjs:160 Attachments/. + .json vault.mjs:487-490 Sources//Source.md + metadata.json vault.mjs:501-505 Sources/pdf-/Source.md, metadata.json, page-NNNN.md, page-NNNN.json, page-NNNN.png pdf.mjs:62,90,103-112 Knowledge/.md vault.mjs:513,527 Visuals//spec.json, preview.svg, index.html, manifest.json, Visual.md tools.mjs:351-366 Style/Voice.md read-only input, controller.mjs:301 _Research/vault.json vault.mjs:8,156 _Research/active.json controller.mjs:203 _Research/writer.lock (+ writer-.tmp) controller.mjs:36-44 _Research/stream/.json vault.mjs:353 _Research/knowledge/.json vault.mjs:518,528 _Research/knowledge//revisions/.md vault.mjs:526 _Research/recovered-edits//-.md vault.mjs:330 _Research/presentation/.request.json / .result.json presentation.mjs:12-15 .obsidian/plugins/pi-research/{main.js,styles.css,manifest.json} install.mjs:14-15 ``` ### Filename-generation rules - Conversation id: `randomUUID()` — vault.mjs:225. `` used as the folder name, validated by `ID = /^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,127}$/` (vault.mjs:6, validateId 27). - Message files: named by the Pi native entry id, `Messages/${id}.json` (vault.mjs:308) and `Messages/${id}.md` (vault.mjs:328). - Attachment id: `` `${sha256.slice(0,48)}-${ext}` `` where `ext` is the MIME-derived extension — vault.mjs:484-487. Content-addressed; no date/slug. - Web source id: `randomUUID()` — vault.mjs:499 → folder `Sources//`. - PDF source id: `` `pdf-${sha256.slice(0,48)}` `` — pdf.mjs:62. - Knowledge filename: `slug(title)` — vault.mjs:513; `slug()` (vault.mjs:533-537): NFKC lowercase, `[^\p{L}\p{N}_-]+`→`-`, strip leading/trailing `-`, `.slice(0,100)`, Windows reserved names (`con|prn|aux|nul|com[1-9]|lpt[1-9]`) prefixed `note-`, empty → `note-`. - Visual id: `randomUUID()` — tools.mjs:344. - Review id / presentation id: `randomUUID()` — review.mjs:115, presentation.mjs:12. - Recovered-edit archive suffix: `hash(previous).slice(0,12)` — vault.mjs:330. ### Frontmatter fields written (produced by `frontmatter()` vault.mjs:97-99: each value `JSON.stringify`-ed, null/undefined keys dropped) - Conversation.md: `research_conversation`, `research_title` — vault.mjs:337. - Message note: `research_conversation`, `research_message`, `research_entry_id`, `research_status`, `created` — vault.mjs:126-131. - Web Source.md: `research_source`, `title`, `url`, `acquired` — vault.mjs:503. - Knowledge note: `research_knowledge` (=true), `research_title`, `research_sources` — vault.mjs:524. - Visual.md: `visual_id` — tools.mjs:356. - PDF Source.md / page-NNNN.md: **no frontmatter** (plain Markdown headings) — pdf.mjs:103,111. ### Write semantics (create-new vs overwrite vs merge) All writes go through `_atomic` (vault.mjs:190-208): write to `...tmp` with `'wx'`, `fsync`, `rename` over target — i.e. **atomic full overwrite, never merge/append**. `fs.mkdir(dirname, {recursive:true})` ensures parent dirs (vault.mjs:194). - Conversation manifest: created at createConversation; `updatedAt` overwritten on each save/session change (vault.mjs:313-315, 364-367). - Message JSON: **immutable** — identical existing record → no write; differing → `ERR_RESEARCH_CONFLICT` "Message is immutable; save a correction under a new ID" (vault.mjs:305-306, conflict() 44). - Conversation.md and per-message .md: **overwrite only when content differs**; a pre-existing differing message .md is first archived to `_Research/recovered-edits/...` (vault.mjs:329-331). - Knowledge note: revision-guarded overwrite. Create-only via `expectedRevision === null`; stale/missing revision → conflict (vault.mjs:520-522); previous content archived under `_Research/knowledge//revisions/.md` (vault.mjs:526). - Attachments: create-only (`_atomic` + `wx`) with hash dedupe; re-import of same hash returns existing record after integrity check (vault.mjs:481-490). - Visuals: every artifact written with `fs.writeFile(..., {flag:'wx'})` = **create-new, fails if exists**; each chart is an immutable snapshot (tools.mjs:360-366). - Companion install: overwrite via temp+rename, but skips when bytes equal (install.mjs:16-25). ## 2. Note-content templating (literal skeletons) `frontmatter()` emits `---\n\n---\n\n`. Sketches, verbatim structure: **Conversation note** (vault.mjs:335-338): ``` --- research_conversation: "" research_title: "" --- # <title> ## [[Conversations/<id>/Messages/<msgId>.md|You|Assistant]] <message text> <attachments><optional \n\n*<status>*><optional \n\n> <review.summary> · [[<reviewPath>|Review notes]]> --- ## [[...]] ``` Section label is `You` for user, `Assistant` for assistant, else the raw role (vault.mjs:333); non-complete status rendered as `*<status>*` (335). **Message note** (vault.mjs:126-131): the frontmatter fields above + `# You|Assistant\n\n<text>` + attachments + `reviewMarkdown` (vault.mjs:123: `\n\n> <summary> · [[<path>|Review notes]]`). **Source note — web** (vault.mjs:503): ``` --- research_source: "<uuid>" title: "<name>" url: "<url>" acquired: "<ISO>" --- # <name> <text> Original: [[Attachments/<id>.<ext>]] (only if an original attachment exists) ``` **Source note — PDF** (pdf.mjs:111, no frontmatter): ``` # <title> [[Attachments/<id>.pdf|Original PDF]] · <N> pages Page text and previews are extracted on demand and stored beside this note. Cite the original PDF with its page number. Source: <url> ``` PDF page note (pdf.mjs:103): `# <title> · page <N>\n\n[[<pdfPath>#page=<N>|Open original page]]\n\n<page text|*No embedded text...*>` (+ truncated note). **Research/knowledge note** (vault.mjs:524): ``` --- research_knowledge: true research_title: "<name>" research_sources: ["<sourceId>", ...] --- # <name> <text> ``` **Visual note** (tools.mjs:350-356): ``` --- visual_id: <uuid> --- # <title> ```research-visual {"path":"Visuals/<uuid>/spec.json"} ``` <details> <summary>Static preview</summary> ![[Visuals/<uuid>/preview.svg]] </details> Sources: [[Sources/<id>/Source|<title>]] · [[...]] [Saved HTML](index.html) ``` **Review note** (review.mjs:158-160): ``` # Evidence review A limited review by <modelId>. This is not independent proof or a check of every claim. <N> claims examined. | Claim | Finding | Reason | | --- | --- | --- | <rows> <evidence bullets "- <source> — <excerpt>"> <clarity + limitations bullets> Model requests: N · Retrieval calls: N · Reported output tokens: N ``` **Index/hub note: none exists.** No `_index.md`, MOC, or hub note is generated anywhere (grep for `index|Hub|MOC|dataview|canvas` over src found only unrelated variable names). The closest thing to an index is `_Research/active.json` (`{conversationId}`) and `listConversations()` walking `Conversations/` (vault.mjs:242-253). ### Obsidian features actually used - **Wikilinks**: yes — message headers, review links, `![[...]]` embeds, visual `Sources:` refs, PDF `[[path#page=N|...]]`. (`[[` emission sites: vault.mjs:115-117,123,335; tools.mjs:349; pdf.mjs:103,111,127) - **Embeds**: `![[<attachment.path>]]` for images (vault.mjs:116), `![[Visuals/<id>/preview.svg]]` for chart static preview (tools.mjs:350). - **Blockquotes**: plain `> summary` for review — **not** an Obsidian callout (vault.mjs:123). - **Tables**: only the Review.md table (review.mjs:158); agent answers may contain tables (presentation.cjs enforces ≤4 columns, `wide-table`). - **Mermaid**: not generated by code; the prompt tells the model to use it (prompt.mjs:12) and presentation.cjs detects/validates it (`hasPresentation`, markdownIssues `dense-diagram`). - **Dataview, tags, canvas**: **none** — no tag (`#tag`) emission, no dataview blocks, no `.canvas` files. - `<details>` HTML disclosure in Visual.md (tools.mjs:350). ## 3. HTML report generation - **Function**: `buildChartDocument(input, options)` — obsidian/visual.cjs:131-139; exported at :140. - **Caller / path**: `saveVisual` → `files['index.html'] = buildChartDocument(normalized, { artifactId: visualId })` — tools.mjs:354; written to vault-relative `Visuals/<visualId>/index.html` via `fs.writeFile(...{flag:'wx'})` — tools.mjs:360. Linked from the note as `[Saved HTML](index.html)` — tools.mjs:356. - **Engine/assets**: no template engine and **no external assets**. CSS is inline `<style>` (visual.cjs:138), JavaScript is an inline `<script nonce>` built by serializing functions: `[escapeXml,formatNumber,niceStep,niceTicks,chartLayout,renderPlotSvg,inspectSvg,chartRuntime].map(fn=>fn.toString()).join('\n')` (visual.cjs:137). CSP header: `default-src 'none'; script-src 'nonce-<token|offline-research-chart>'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; connect-src 'none'; img-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'` (visual.cjs:138). Body: `<h1>`, `#legend`, `#plot` (pre-rendered `renderPreviewSvg`), `#tooltip`, optional caption `<p>`, `<details><summary>Sources</summary><ul>` external `<a>` links, `<details><summary>View data</summary>` table of series/x/y rows. It embeds the spec via `scriptJson(spec)` and config `{token, artifactId}`. - **JSON/JS manifests describing artifacts**: - `Visuals/<id>/manifest.json` (tools.mjs:348): `{schemaVersion:1, visualId, title, conversationId, sourceIds, illustrative, createdAt, specPath}`. - `Visuals/<id>/spec.json` = normalized chart spec (tools.mjs:352). - Conversation `Conversations/<id>/manifest.json`: `{version,id,title,createdAt,updatedAt,sessionFile}` (vault.mjs:227). - Companion plugin manifest `.obsidian/plugins/pi-research/manifest.json` (obsidian/manifest.json; id `pi-research`, name `Discover`, v0.6.3). - Review `report.json` (review.mjs:155-156) describes the review artifact, not a published HTML index. - The plugin's live rendering uses `obsidian/main.js` (built from plugin.cjs) with a token-bound iframe; `_Research/presentation/` request/result files are transient (presentation.mjs:12-15, 24-25 cleanup). ## 4. Sources: storage, dedupe, citations, backlink - **Schema** — web: `Sources/<uuid>/metadata.json` = `{version:1,id,title,url,acquiredAt,mimeType,textHash,original}` (vault.mjs:500) plus `Source.md` (frontmatter above). PDF: `Sources/pdf-<hash48>/metadata.json` = `{version:1,id,title,url,acquiredAt,mimeType:'application/pdf',original,sha256,totalPages,extractionVersion}` (pdf.mjs:110) plus `Source.md` and `page-NNNN.{md,json,png}` caches (pdf.mjs:90-104). Attachments: `Attachments/<id>.json` = `{id,path,mimeType,name,size,sha256}` (vault.mjs:489). - **Dedupe key**: web sources are **not deduped** — a fresh `randomUUID` per `saveSource` (vault.mjs:499). PDFs are deduped by original-byte sha256 (`sourceId = pdf-<sha256.slice(0,48)>`, pdf.mjs:62) and page caches validated against `sha256` + `extractionVersion` (pdf.mjs:68-72). Attachments deduped by sha256 (vault.mjs:484-487) with integrity check (vault.mjs:483). - **Citation into the answer**: no code inserts citations into the lead answer; the prompt instructs the model: "Cite original sources beside claims with Markdown links" (prompt.mjs:12). Returned tool payloads expose `sourceId`/`path` for the model (tools.mjs fetch_source result ~:406). Visual tool returns an exact Markdown block whose `Sources:` line is `[[Sources/<id>/Source|<title>]]` joined by ` · ` (tools.mjs:349). PDF reads return a `citation` field per page: `[[<pdfPath>#page=<N>|<title> · p. <N>]]` (pdf.mjs:127). - **Link back to the source note**: constructed only as wikilinks — `[[Sources/${source.id}/Source|title]]` (tools.mjs:349), `Original: [[<attachment.path>]]` (vault.mjs:503), `[[<pdfPath>|Original PDF]]` / `[[<pdfPath>#page=N|...]]` (pdf.mjs:111,103,127). There is no reverse field written into the source note pointing at citing answers. ## 5. Cross-note linking / vault-wide scan & index - **Between conversations**: none. Fork/continue write JSON pointers only — `Conversations/<id>/origin.json` = `{kind:'fork', conversationId, entryId}` (controller.mjs:239) or `{kind:'note', path, revision}` (controller.mjs:220). `select()` reads origin.json but only consumes `kind==='note'` to set `contextNote` (controller.mjs:110-113); no wikilink or backlink is added to either conversation note. - **Tag-based grouping**: none (no tags emitted anywhere). - **Visual↔source links**: `Visuals/<id>/manifest.json.sourceIds` (JSON) and the note's `Sources:` wikilinks (tools.mjs:348-350). - **Search over existing notes**: `ResearchVault.search` (vault.mjs:437-455). Cost: calls `_notePaths()` (vault.mjs:376-396) which walks the **whole vault top-down, capped at 1500 files** (`if (found.length >= 1500) return`, :379), skips hidden / `_research` / `sessions` / `node_modules` parts via `isNotePath` (:101), then for each `.md` **stats and reads** it, skips >2 MiB, and scans the **first 128000 chars** (`bounded = text.slice(0,128000)`, :445), explicitly skipping `Conversations/*/Conversation.md` (:441). Scoring is term-count based (:452). **No caching and no persisted index** — every search re-walks and re-reads. `readNote` title resolution also triggers `_notePaths()` and, when no filename match, reads every ≤2 MiB candidate to compare titles (vault.mjs:415-421). - Persistent state is only `_Research/active.json` (last conversation pointer, controller.mjs:203) and the per-conversation/system JSON sidecars; there is no vault-wide index file. ## 6. Vault path resolution / validation / folder creation - **`vaultRoot(input)`** — vault.mjs:98-105: `fs.realpath(path.resolve(input))`; requires an existing directory; requires a resolvable `.obsidian` directory **inside** the root (`within(root, obsidian)`); errors: "Select an existing Obsidian vault" (empty input), "Vault path is not a directory", "The selected folder must contain its own .obsidian directory". Unreadable/EACCES paths propagate from realpath/stat. - **`ResearchVault.bind(input,{scholarRoots})`** — vault.mjs:143-159: calls `vaultRoot`, rejects same/nested Scholar roots via `potentialRealPath` + `within` ("Discover and Scholar vaults must be separate, non-nested folders"), serializes on `bind:<root>`, creates `_Research/vault.json` = `{version:1,id:randomUUID(),createdAt}` if absent (vault.mjs:153-157), validates id. - **`ResearchVault.open(input, expectedId)`** — vault.mjs:162-171: `vaultRoot` + read/validate `_Research/vault.json` (`validVaultMeta`, :107-110, error "Invalid research vault metadata"); mismatch with saved id → "Discover vault identity does not match the saved binding". - **Linked-vault flow** — extension.mjs:46-53 `linkedVault`: `readConfig()`; if null throws "Link an existing vault first: /discover vault ...", then `ResearchVault.open(config.vaultRoot, config.vaultId)` and `bind`. `/discover vault` handler: bind → `installCompanion` → `writeConfig` (extension.mjs:104-109). - **Config pointer** — config.mjs:7-20: path `join(process.env.PI_RESEARCH_CONFIG_DIR || ~/.pi/agent/research, 'config.json')`; `readConfig` requires `version===1`, string `vaultRoot`, string `vaultId`, returns null on ENOENT; `writeConfig` writes atomically with `mode 0o600`. - **Folder existence/creation & path safety**: - `relativePath` (vault.mjs:70-90) rejects absolute/`..`/`:`-containing/var-segment-`. `ERR_PATH_ESCAPE`. - `safePath` (vault.mjs:175-188) re-realpaths root, rejects "The linked vault location has changed", resolves existing symlinks/junctions component-wise, throws `ERR_PATH_ESCAPE` "Symlink or junction escapes the linked vault", returns the non-existent tail unchanged. It does **not** create anything. - `_atomic` creates missing parent dirs (`fs.mkdir(path.dirname(target),{recursive:true})`, vault.mjs:194). Extra `mkdir` sites: conversation sessions (vault.mjs:228), `_Research` for the lock (controller.mjs:37), Reviews dir (review.mjs:117), `Visuals/` and `Visuals/<id>` (tools.mjs:358-359), plugin dir (install.mjs:16). - `optional()` (vault.mjs:60-63) swallows only `ENOENT` (returns null); all other FS errors surface. E.g. missing `_Research/active.json` is tolerated (controller.mjs:61), missing `_Research/vault.json` in `open` is not. ### Uncertain / not found - No code path writes any conversation-linking wikilink, tag, dataview block, or canvas file; grep over `src/` and `obsidian/` found none. - Web `saveSource` has no URL-based cache/dedupe mechanism anywhere (searched `Source.md`, `metadata.json`, `saveSource` callers); each `fetch_source` creates a new `Sources/<uuid>/`. - The companion's live reading pane (obsidian/main.js/plugin.cjs) consumes the chart token protocol but was not exhaustively read here; the offline HTML report producer is fully identified in visual.cjs.

data.summary: pi-discover has 94 `node:test` tests across 10 `.mjs` files plus one out-of-band Playwright harness (`tests/browser/formatting.cjs`, not run by `npm test`). `npm test` = `node --test tests/*.test.mjs` (package.json:16). No test touches the network or a real LLM: model calls go to pi-ai's scripted `fauxProvider`, HTTP is injected via `fetchImpl`/`lookupImpl`, and the Obsidian host API is stubbed. 33 of the 94 tests are gated by `{ skip: !sdk }` (runtime 16/17, review 17/18) and only run when `PI_RESEARCH_SDK` points at an installed Pi dist — so a bare `npm test` executes 61 and skips 33. A rewrite of the response engine, prompts, note templates, or companion markup will break a large, precisely-anchored surface: literal prompt phrases (/ Ask /i, /latest corrections/), the imported `ANSWER_GUIDE`/`RESEARCH_COMPACTION_GUIDE` injection contract, literal stream phase strings, the `research-visual` fence + `<details><summary>Static preview</summary>` note template, `research_entry_id` frontmatter, `Visuals/<id>/{Visual.md,index.html,manifest.json,preview.svg,spec.json}`, and the companion's view/processor ids.
data.architecture: Layered: (1) pure-ish units — `src/config.mjs` (parseCommand/scholarOwnsInput), `src/context.mjs` (recall/brief/compaction guide/settings), `src/review.mjs` (shouldReview/evidencePacket/parseReview/limits), `src/presentation.mjs`; (2) vault persistence — `src/vault.mjs` (ResearchVault: confinement, immutable messages, Conversation.md projection, streams, knowledge revisions) exercised against real temp dirs; (3) tools — `src/tools.mjs` (11 tools) with injected fetch/lookup; (4) orchestration — `src/controller.mjs` + `src/session-store.mjs` driven through the real Pi SDK with a scripted local provider; (5) extension plumbing — `src/extension.mjs` tested with a fully faked dependency object; (6) companion — `obsidian/main.js` (esbuild bundle of plugin.cjs+visual.cjs+presentation.cjs) tested via `vm` with a stub `obsidian` module, and `obsidian/visual.cjs`/`presentation.cjs` tested directly; (7) browser QA — real bundle + real styles.css + local Mermaid in headless Edge with a fake vault adapter.

data.architecture: Runtime target: the user runs `pi`, which is `%LOCALAPPDATA%\pi-node\current\pi.cmd` shelling to `node .../pi-coding-agent/dist/bundle/cli.js` (single esbuild bundle, version 0.85.1). The bundle also serves the peer packages @earendil-works/pi-tui, /pi-ai, /pi-agent-core, typebox as *virtual modules* (chunk-JVUZSMYM.js:1066) — no such directories exist under node_modules, so runtime imports work but TypeScript types for pi-tui are not on disk. Extensions are jiti-loaded TS modules discovered from ~/.pi/agent/extensions/*.ts|*/index.ts, .pi/extensions/..., settings `packages` entries, or a package's `pi.extensions` manifest. The extension talks to the host only through ExtensionAPI (events + registrations) and per-call ExtensionContext/ExtensionCommandContext; the host owns the model turn, the TUI and the session file. Consequently the pi-discover rewrite has two viable orchestration strategies inside one extension process: (a) in-process, no-session model calls via ctx.modelRegistry.complete(model, context, options) or ctx.modelRegistry.getProvider(p).streamSimple(...) (scholar's approach: bounded tool loop, own AbortController, Promise.all concurrency), or (b) spawn sibling `pi --mode json -p --no-session --model X --tools ... [--append-system-prompt file] "Task: ..."` child processes and parse JSONL (the bundled subagent example). The user-visible surface is the `/discover` command plus a CustomEditor input lock and footer/widget progress; a final Markdown note is written directly to the vault by the extension, and/or the answer can be injected with pi.sendMessage({triggerTurn:true}) so Pi renders it as an assistant message.

## 2. scholar: exact ExtensionAPI calls at registration

`scholar/index.ts` default factory receives `pi: ExtensionAPI`. It registers **1 command and 2 tools** (not 11):

- Command — `index.ts:490`:
```ts
pi.registerCommand("scholar", {
  description: "Select a PDF book and explicitly start isolated Learn, Exam, or Tutor mode",
  getArgumentCompletions: async (prefix) => ... ,
  handler: (args: string, ctx: ExtensionCommandContext) => { warningContext = ctx; return handleScholarCommand(args, ctx, coordinator); },
});
```
- Tool `scholar` — `tool-controller.ts:830-836`: `pi.registerTool({ name: "scholar", label: "Scholar", description: <long literal>, parameters: ScholarParams, executionMode: "sequential", renderShell: "self", execute(...), renderCall(...) @1241, renderResult(...) @1253 })`.
- Tool `scholar_quiz` — `quiz.ts:509`, name constant `quiz-contract.ts:11` `export const SCHOLAR_QUIZ_TOOL_NAME = "scholar_quiz" as const;`; has `renderCall` @572 and `renderResult` @581.

**Event hooks** (all in `index.ts`): `session_start` :67, `before_agent_start` :86 (returns `{ systemPrompt: event.systemPrompt + "\n\n" + instructions }`), `input` :145, `agent_end` :163, `message_update` :171, `tool_execution_start`/`tool_execution_end` :172-173, `agent_settled` :175, `session_shutdown` :256, `message_end` :270, `tool_call` :299 (returns `{ block: true, reason }` to veto), `tool_execution_update` :406, `tool_result` :432 (returns `{ content: [...event.content, {type:"text", text}] }`).

**Never called:** `registerFlag`, `registerShortcut`, `registerProvider`, `registerMessageRenderer`, `registerEntryRenderer`, `registerMarkdownTransformer` (grep for `pi.<that>` across scholar returned nothing).

**Input takeover (`input-lock.ts`, full file read):**
- Mechanism: replace the editor factory with a subclass of Pi's `CustomEditor`, imported from the SDK:
```ts
import { CustomEditor, type ExtensionContext, type ExtensionUIContext } from "@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent";
import { matchesKey, truncateToWidth, type EditorTheme, type KeybindingsManager, type TUI } from "@earendil-works/pi-tui";

class ScholarLockedEditor extends CustomEditor {
  handleInput(data: string): void {
    if (this.appKeys.matches(data, "app.interrupt") || matchesKey(data, "escape")) this.interrupt();
  }
  render(width: number): string[] {
    return [this.borderColor(truncateToWidth(` Scholar · ${this.label()} · input paused · Esc interrupts `, Math.max(1, width), ""))];
  }
}
```
- Guard (throws if unavailable):
```ts
if (typeof ui?.setEditorComponent !== "function" || typeof ui?.getEditorComponent !== "function")
  throw new Error("Scholar requires Pi's getEditorComponent/setEditorComponent APIs to pause interactive chat input. Update to a compatible Pi host and restart, then retry.");
```
- Acquire: `currentFactory = ui.getEditorComponent()`; push a `Symbol("scholar-input-lock")` token; on first token set `lockUi`, `previousEditorFactory`, `installedEditorFactory = (tui, theme, keybindings) => new ScholarLockedEditor(...)`; then `ui.setEditorComponent(installedEditorFactory)` and verify `ui.getEditorComponent() === installedEditorFactory`.
- Release returns an idempotent closure; the prior factory is restored only when the last token releases **and** `restoreUi.getEditorComponent() === installedFactory`. `releaseAllInputLocks()` clears the map and restores. Default label literal is `"loading"`.
- The lock additionally swallows non-key input because `render()` shows only the paused line; `interrupt` calls `ctx.abort()`.
- The `input` hook is a second layer: on a busy run it re-inserts the draft with `ctx.ui.setEditorText(event.text)` and returns `{ action: "handled" as const }`.

## 4. scholar: how it runs its own model calls

No SDK session, no child process, no `subagent` API. It calls the **active registry in-process**, which is what preserves Pi's providers, OAuth, headers and credentials (comment at `review-runtime.ts:165-168`).

Signatures (`SDK/dist/core/model-registry.d.ts`):
```ts
complete<TApi extends Api>(model: Model<TApi>, context: Context, options?: ModelsApiStreamOptions<TApi>): Promise<AssistantMessage>;
getProvider(provider: string): Provider | undefined;
getApiKeyAndHeaders(model: Model<Api>): Promise<ResolvedRequestAuth>;   // {ok:true, apiKey?, headers?, baseUrl?, env?} | {ok:false, error}
```
- Non-reasoning path — `review-runtime.ts:298-301`:
```ts
response = await abortable(
  Promise.race([options.modelRegistry.complete(options.model, context, requestOptions), stallPromise]),
  signal,
);
```
with `requestOptions = { signal, maxTokens, timeoutMs, maxRetries: 0, sessionId: requestSessionId, transport: "sse" as const }` (`:296`).
- Reasoning path — `review-runtime.ts:318-321` + stream consumption at `:355-359`:
```ts
const provider = options.modelRegistry.getProvider!(options.model.provider);
const auth = await options.modelRegistry.getApiKeyAndHeaders!(options.model, signal);
const stream = provider.streamSimple(requestModel, context, { ...requestOptions, apiKey, headers, env, reasoning });
[response] = await abortable(Promise.all([Promise.race([stream.result(), stallPromise]), observe()]), signal);
```
- It builds its own `Context` (`{ systemPrompt, messages: [{role:"user", content: prompt, timestamp}], tools: [{name, description, parameters}] }` @:239-243), runs a bounded tool loop (`maxTurns`, `maxToolCalls`, `Value.Check` arg validation, `review-runtime.ts:439-470`), aborts with its own `AbortController`, and finally `cleanupSessionResources(requestSessionId)` (`:3`, `:468`).
- **Parallelism** is plain JS: `review-layer.ts:546`
```ts
await Promise.all(Array.from({ length: Math.min(REVIEW_CONCURRENCY, packets.length) }, worker));
```
- **Alternative (bundled example, not used by scholar):** `examples/extensions/subagent/index.ts` spawns a child `pi` per worker — args built at `:303`: `["--mode", "json", "-p", "--no-session", ...("--model" ?), ...("--thinking" ?), ...("--tools" ?), "--append-system-prompt", tmpPromptPath, `Task: ${task}`]` — parses JSONL `message_end` events, `MAX_PARALLEL_TASKS = 8`, `MAX_CONCURRENCY = 4`.
- **Third option (SDK docs):** `createAgentSession({ model, tools, sessionManager: SessionManager.inMemory(), modelRuntime })` → `session.prompt(text, options)`, `session.subscribe(listener)`, `session.steer/followUp`, `session.abort()` — plus `createAgentSessionRuntime()` for new/switch/fork/import. `AgentSession` has no session-replacement methods; those live on `AgentSessionRuntime`.

**No `subagent`/`spawnSubagent` API exists on the host.** Checked: `grep -i 'subagent|Subagent|subAgent|runSubagent'` over the whole `SDK/dist` tree returned **no matches**.

## 5. Session open / resume / switch and extension state lifecycle

**From an extension, session control lives on `ExtensionCommandContext`** (`SDK/dist/core/extensions/types.d.ts`, interface declared after `ExtensionContext`):
```ts
newSession(options?: { parentSession?: string; setup?: (sessionManager: SessionManager) => Promise<void>; withSession?: (ctx: ReplacedSessionContext) => Promise<void>; }): Promise<{ cancelled: boolean }>;
fork(entryId: string, options?: { position?: "before" | "at"; withSession?: ... }): Promise<{ cancelled: boolean }>;
navigateTree(targetId: string, options?: { summarize?; customInstructions?; replaceInstructions?; label? }): Promise<{ cancelled: boolean }>;
switchSession(sessionPath: string, options?: { withSession?: ... }): Promise<{ cancelled: boolean }>;
reload(): Promise<void>;
waitForIdle(): Promise<void>;
getSystemPromptOptions(): BuildSystemPromptOptions;
```
`ReplacedSessionContext extends ExtensionCommandContext` and adds `sendMessage(...)` / `sendUserMessage(...)`.

**Events (`ExtensionAPI.on` overloads at `types.d.ts:907-942`; payloads defined above it):**
- `SessionStartEvent` — `reason: "startup" | "reload" | "new" | "resume" | "fork"`, `previousSessionFile?`.
- `SessionBeforeSwitchEvent` — `reason: "new" | "resume"`, `targetSessionFile?` (cancellable via `SessionBeforeSwitchResult`).
- `SessionShutdownEvent` — `reason: "quit" | "reload" | "new" | "resume" | "fork"`, `targetSessionFile?`.
- Also `session_before_fork`, `session_before_compact`/`session_compact`/`session_compact_failed`, `session_before_tree`/`session_tree`, `session_info_changed`, `resources_discover` (`reason: "startup" | "reload"`).

**Documented semantics (docs/extensions.md):**
- `:431-433` — "After a successful switch or new-session action, pi emits `session_shutdown` for the old extension instance, reloads and rebinds extensions for the new session, then emits `session_start` with `reason: "new" | "resume"` and `previousSessionFile`."
- `:449-450` — same for fork/clone with `reason: "fork"`.
- `:224` — "Register an idempotent `session_shutdown` handler to close any session-scoped resources you start." Factories may run without a session; do not start background resources from the factory.
- `:1303-1325` — `ctx.reload()` runs the same flow as `/reload`: emits `session_shutdown`, reloads resources, emits `session_start {reason:"reload"}`; the running handler continues in the **old** call frame and must treat reload as terminal (`await ctx.reload(); return;`).
- `:1264-1269` — `withSession` runs only after the old session's `session_shutdown`, runtime teardown, rebind and the new instance's `session_start`; old `pi`/`ctx` are stale; only the passed `ctx` is safe.

**Persistence of extension state:**
- Write: `pi.appendEntry<T>(customType: string, data?: T): void` (`types.d.ts`, ExtensionAPI) — custom entries are NOT in LLM context. scholar uses it at `runtime-coordinator.ts:463` with `SCHOLAR_SESSION_STATE_TYPE = "scholar-active-v3"` (`runtime-session.ts:11`).
- Restore: iterate `ctx.sessionManager.getBranch()` / `getEntries()` in `session_start`. `ReadonlySessionManager` (`session-manager.d.ts:140`) exposes `getCwd|getSessionDir|getSessionId|getSessionFile (@:209)|getLeafId(@:240)|getLeafEntry|getEntry|getLabel|getBranch(@:262)|buildContextEntries|getHeader|getEntries(@:282)|getTree|getSessionName`.
- scholar's `session_start` handler (`index.ts:67-84`) resets everything: `releaseAllInputLocks()`, `deactivateSession()`, `runtimeSession.reset()`, `toolController.resetTransientState()`; and `session_shutdown` (`:256-268`) releases every run/lock and calls `ctx.ui.setWorkingMessage()`.

- MAX ITERATIONS: none. Grep for `maxIterations|maxTurns|maxSteps` across PI_AGENT/dist/**/*.d.ts returned NO option; the loop is unbounded and terminates on no-more-tool-calls / early-termination / abort.
- Abort: Agent.abort() (agent.d.ts), AgentSession.abort() (agent-session.d.ts:444), ctx.abort() (types.d.ts:1301), and AbortSignal passed to tools/streams (options.signal, execute(..., signal, ...)).
- Tool result feedback: toolcall_end → execute → AgentToolResult → tool_result/tool_execution_end events → toolResult message appended to context → next LLM call (docs/sdk.md:249-333). ToolResultEventResult can replace content/details/isError/usage; terminate:true on every finalized batch result stops after that batch (PI_AGENT types.d.ts:317-331).
- Loop control hooks on AgentLoopConfig (PI_AGENT types.d.ts:~180-260) / AgentOptions (agent.d.ts): shouldStopAfterTurn(context): boolean, prepareNextTurn(context), getSteeringMessages(), getFollowUpMessages(), beforeToolCall ({block:true}), afterToolCall (override), toolExecution.
- Extension running its own loop: (a) call session.prompt() repeatedly; (b) construct your own Agent and drive prompt()/continue() with custom hooks; (c) skip the agent and call modelRuntime.complete()/stream() per request in a loop you control (planner → N researchers in parallel → synthesizer). (c) is the cleanest fit for pi-discover.

- Only ONE command (`/discover`) is needed; the concurrent planner/researcher/synthesizer calls live in its handler, not in registered model tools.
- Emit progress via ctx.ui.setStatus/setWidget/notify; write the final Markdown note from the handler with plain Node fs (optionally withFileMutationQueue).

# Discover overhaul — chat answers that become Obsidian notes

## Context

`pi-discover` is a Pi extension (`pi install git:github.com/BasamAhmed640/pi-discover`, currently v0.6.3) that answers questions in the Pi composer and writes results into a linked Obsidian vault. Its current shape is the problem: two effort modes (`ask`/`deep`), a scripted evidence reviewer, an installed Obsidian companion plugin that renders answers as sandboxed-HTML chart iframes and `.html` "Reports", a browser-rendered layout checker, conversation forking, 11 model tools, and ~4.5 kLOC of source plus a committed plugin bundle.

The overhaul replaces that product shape: `/discover` becomes a chat — you type a question, the extension runs a small parallel research crew itself, streams back a short direct answer in the terminal, and appends a dense, information-heavy section to one Markdown note per chat in the vault. No modes, no plugin, no HTML, no layout checking, no forking. Vault linking and reconnect-to-a-linked-vault are kept exactly as they work today. Sources become real notes in the vault and are cited by wiki-link. Answers are concise and unsentimental: information first, no assistant warmth.

Decisions already fixed by the user: short brief in Pi + dense note in Obsidian; one running note per chat; adaptive agent fan-out; keep chats + images + PDFs (drop forking); related-chat links now via a cheap incremental index.

## Verified facts this plan relies on

Run of `main` @ `8195ae8a` fetched read-only into session scratch (`local://pi-discover-src/`); Pi SDK/SDK docs read from the installed `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@0.85.1`.

- Extension contract: `ExtensionAPI` gives `registerCommand`, `registerTool`, `on('input'|'session_start'|'session_shutdown'|…)`, `sendMessage({customType, content, display}, {triggerTurn})`, `appendEntry`, `registerMessageRenderer`, `setActiveTools`; `ExtensionContext` gives `ui` (`setStatus`, `setWidget`, `setEditorComponent`, `select`, `confirm`, `input`, `notify`, `getEditorText`, `setEditorText`), `model`, `thinkingLevel`, `modelRegistry`, `sessionManager`, `hasUI`, `isIdle()`.
- `ModelRegistry.complete(model, context, options)` and `ModelRuntime`'s `streamSimple(model, context, options)` take a plain `{systemPrompt, messages, tools}` context — stateless single-shot calls, no session required. ## Approach

Ordered so the tree stays valid after each step: new modules land first (unreferenced), then the host surface switches to them, then the obsolete surface is deleted, then tests/docs.

### Step 1 — Land the new vault layer

New files: `src/vault.mjs`, `src/index-store.mjs`, `src/notes.mjs`.

**Folder and file contract** (all under the linked vault root; `_` prefix marks machine-owned dirs):

```text
_discover/vault.json         {"version":1,"id":<uuid>,"createdAt":<iso>}
_discover/active.json        {"version":1,"chatId":<uuid>}
_discover/writer.lock        {"version":1,"pid":<n>,"host":"<os.hostname()>","startedAt":<iso>,"token":<uuid>}
_discover/index.json         {"version":1,"updatedAt":<iso>,
                              "chats":{"<chatId>":{"path","title","topics":[],"sources":[<sourceId>],"updatedAt"}},
                              "sources":{"<sourceId>":{"path","url","title","kind":"web|pdf","hash","retrievedAt"}}}
_discover/chats/<chatId>.json {"version":1,"id","title","notePath","createdAt","updatedAt","model","topics":[],"sources":[],"turns":<n>}
_discover/pdf/<sha48>/…      extracted page text + page PNG cache (kept from current pdf.mjs)
Chats/<YYYY-MM-DD> <Title>.md
Sources/<Title> (<hash8>).md
Style/Voice.md               read-only, user-owned, optional, ≤4000 chars injected into the writer prompt
```

`src/notes.mjs` exports pure builders/parsers (no fs):

- `frontmatter(fields) -> string` — YAML block, keys in fixed order.
- `callout(kind, title, bodyLines, {collapsed}) -> string` — `> [!kind]- Title` + `> ` lines; emits `>` for blank lines inside the callout.
- `questionHeading(index, text) -> string` — `## <n>. <text>` (question verbatim, single line; newlines collapsed to spaces).
- `appendExchange(noteText, exchange) -> string` — appends `\n\n` + heading + provenance callout + body section before the trailing related-marker block when present, otherwise at end.
- `relatedBlock(entries) -> string` — wrapped in `<!-- discover:related:start -->` / `<!-- discover:related:end -->`.
- `rewriteBlock(noteText, marker, block) -> string` — replace between markers; missing markers → append at end.
- `splitExchanges(noteText) -> [{question, body}]` — split on `^## ` headings.
- `recentExchanges(noteText, count, charBudget) -> string` — last N exchanges, trimmed to the last `charBudget` characters on whole lines.
- `normalizeObsidianMarkdown(text) -> string` — outside fenced code blocks convert `\(…\)` → `$…$` and `\[…\]` → `$$…$$`; collapse 3+ blank lines to 2; strip trailing whitespace; guarantee a trailing newline.
- `sanitizeTitle(text) -> string` — strip `[\\/:*?"<>|#^\[\]]`, collapse whitespace, trim trailing dots/spaces, cap 80 chars, empty → `Untitled chat`.
- `sourceFileName(title, hash8) -> string`, `chatFileName(date, title) -> string`, `sourceRef(sourceId, title, hash8) -> "[[Sources/<Title> (<hash8>)|<Title>]]"` — the exact wiki-link string handed to the model.
- `uniquePath(exists, dir, baseName, ext) -> string` — appends ` 2`, ` 3`… on collision.

`src/vault.mjs` exports `openVault(root, {scholarRoots}) -> Vault` and class `Vault`:

- `ensure()` — create `_discover/`, `_discover/chats/`, `Chats/`, `Sources/`; write `_discover/vault.json` when absent, adopting the id from `_Research/vault.json` when that legacy file exists and parses (keeps an existing linked vault's identity stable). Identity mismatch against the stored pointer throws `'Discover vault identity does not match the saved binding'`.
- `acquireLock()` / `releaseLock()` / `unlockStale()` — token/pid/host lock. Stale when `host === os.hostname()` and the pid is not alive → steal silently; a live lock from another host throws `'This vault is being written by <host>. Close that Pi instance or run /discover unlock.'`.
- `writeFile(relPath, text)` / `readFile(relPath)` — atomic temp-file + rename, `mkdir -p`, per-path promise serialization, path-escape and symlink guard (copy the guard rules from the current `src/vault.mjs:safePath`).
- `storySource({url, title, kind, text, hash}) -> {id, path, ref, title, reused}` — dedupe key `sha256(normalizedUrl)` for `web` (lowercase scheme+host, no fragment, drop `utm_*`/`fbclid`/`gclid`/`ref`, remaining query params sorted) and `sha256(fileBytes)` for `pdf`; reuse the existing `Sources/<Title> (<hash8>).md` when the id is already indexed by recording a new reference entry, else write it (template below).
- `noteSourceReference(sourceId, chatPath)` — rewrite the source note's `## Referenced by` block between `<!-- discover:refs:start -->`/`:end -->` with `- [[<chat note>]]` lines, deduped, sorted.
- `relatedChats(chatId, {limit:3})` — from the index: other chats with `sharedSources >= 2 || sharedTopics >= 3`, ties broken by most recent `updatedAt`.
- `upsertIndexChat(record)` / `upsertIndexSource(record)` / `setActive(chatId)` / `getActive()` / `getChat(id)` / `listChats()` / `saveChat(record)`.

**Chat note template** (`Chats/<date> <Title>.md`):

```markdown
---
discover: chat
chat: <chatId>
title: <title>
created: <iso>
updated: <iso>
topics: [a, b]
tags: [discover/a, discover/b]
sources: 3
model: <provider/model-id>
---

# <title>

## 1. <question 1 verbatim>

> [!info]- Asked 2026-09-17 09:12 · 3 sources · <provider/model-id>
> [[Sources/AlphaEvolve (1b5c7b49)|AlphaEvolve]] · [[Sources/…]]

<note body>

<!-- discover:related:start -->
> [!link]- Related
> - [[Chats/2026-09-14 …]] — shares [[Sources/…]]
<!-- discover:related:end -->
```

Second and later turns append the same `## <n>. <question>` + provenance callout + body block; only the current note's related block is rewritten per turn. Existing content outside the markers is never modified.

**Source note template** (`Sources/<Title> (<hash8>).md`):

```markdown
---
discover: source
title: <page title>
url: <url>
kind: web|pdf
retrieved: <iso>
hash: <sha256/16>
---

# <title>

<readable text; for kind:pdf, `## Page <n>` sections>

<!-- discover:refs:start -->
## Referenced by
- [[Chats/2026-09-17 …]]
<!-- discover:refs:end -->
```

**Vault pointer**: keep the existing machine-local path and fields verbatim — `join(process.env.PI_RESEARCH_CONFIG_DIR || join(homedir(), '.pi','agent','research'), 'config.json')`, `{version:1, vaultRoot, vaultId}`, mode `0o600`, atomic write. `src/config.mjs` also keeps `scholarRoots()` (Scholar pointer + `PI_SCHOLAR_OBSIDIAN_ROOT`) so `/discover vault` still rejects the Scholar vault and nested/aliased roots with the existing messages.

Empty/missing/error handling: missing vault pointer → the existing hint string `'Link an existing vault first: /discover vault "C:\\path\\to\\Vault"'`; vault path missing or not a directory → `'That vault folder does not exist.'`; `_discover/index.json` unreadable/corrupt → rebuild from `_discover/chats/*.json` and `Sources/*.md` frontmatter (index is derived data, never authoritative); a chat record whose note file is gone → drop the chat from `listChats()` and report `'<title>: note file is missing; the chat was skipped.'`.

### Step 2 — Land the research layer

New files: `src/tools.mjs` (web only), `src/research.mjs`, `src/citations.mjs`.

`src/tools.mjs` exports `createWebTools({vault, model, fetchImpl, lookupImpl}) -> Tool[]` with exactly two tools, each `{name, description, parameters, execute}` in the plain shape `modelRegistry.complete` expects:

| Tool | Parameters | Returns |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `web_search` | `query: string (≤500, required)`, `limit: integer 1–8 (default 5)` | `{results: [{title, url, snippet}]}` |
| `fetch_source` | `url: string (≤4096, required)`, `refresh: boolean` | `{sourceId, ref, title, url, text (≤24000 chars, `truncated` flag on the result), cached: boolean}` |

Keep the current hand-rolled keyless search + SSRF-guarded `pinnedFetch` implementation (the web-only subset of today's `src/tools.mjs`, unchanged in behavior: DNS-pinned lookup, size cap, redirect cap, content-type allowlist, HTML→text extraction). `fetch_source` resolves through the vault index first: an already-stored URL returns the stored text with `cached: true` unless `refresh: true`, in which case it refetches and rewrites the source note. Every successful fetch calls `vault.storySource(...)`, so the returned `sourceId`/`ref` is already backed by a file in `Sources/`. Failure returns `{error: '<kind>', url}` (`blocked`, `http-<code>`, `too-large`, `timeout`, `unsupported-type`) — never throws into the loop.

`src/research.mjs` exports:

- `route({model, registry, thinkingLevel, question, recentContext, signal}) -> {research: boolean, queries: string[], reason: string}` — one `streamSimple` call, tools `[]`, ≤400 output tokens, 45 s timeout; malformed JSON → one retry with `"Return only the JSON object."`; second failure → `{research:false, queries:[], reason:'routing failed'}`.
- `runWorker({model, registry, thinkingLevel, query, tools, signal, onProgress}) -> {query, findings:[{claim, quote, sourceId, ref}], gaps:string[], toolCalls:number, tokens:number}` — the bounded loop, adapted verbatim in structure from `scholar/review-runtime.ts:180-400`: build `context = {systemPrompt, messages:[{role:'user', content: prompt}], tools}`; loop `MAX_TURNS = 8`; each turn call `provider.streamSimple(requestModel, context, {reasoning, signal, maxTokens: min(6000, remaining), sessionId, transport:'sse', maxRetries:0})`, race against a 90 s no-event stall watchdog, append the assistant message, execute each `toolCall` block through the tool map, push `{role:'toolResult', …}` messages; stop on no tool calls. Enforce `MAX_TOOL_CALLS = 6` and `MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS = 12000` per worker; on limit or provider error, return the packet with `gaps:['<reason>']` rather than throwing. Parse the final text as JSON; malformed → one repair request; still malformed → `{query, findings:[], gaps:['packet malformed']}`.
- `runCrew({queries, …}) -> packets[]` — `Promise.all` over at most 4 queries (`MAX_WORKERS = 4`); each worker gets its own `AbortController` linked to the turn signal; a rejected worker becomes `{query, findings:[], gaps:['<error>']}`.

Packets carry `ref` strings copied from `fetch_source` results; `citations.mjs` and the writer both use that exact string.

`src/citations.mjs` exports `checkCitations(noteBody, allowedRefs) -> {body, unresolved: string[], cited: number}`: find `\[\[Sources/[^\]|]+(\|[^\]]*)?\]\]`, keep only those whose target matches an `allowedRefs` entry (this turn's sources plus sources already indexed for this chat), and replace every other occurrence with its display text as plain text plus ` (unresolved source)`. `cited` counts surviving links. No model call.

### Step 3 — Land the answer layer

New file: `src/answer.mjs` — the writer prompt, the outcome parser, and the writer call.

- `WRITER_PROMPT` (literal, assembled with the context sections appended):

```
You write one answer for a competent reader who wants the answer, not a lesson.
The user's question is in the current Obsidian vault conversation. The host prints the question above
your note body and shows your brief in the terminal.

Return exactly three sections in this order, each marker alone on its own line:

<<<META>>>
{"title": "...", "topics": ["..."], "confidence": "high|medium|low", "open": ["..."]}
<<<BRIEF>>>
<2-5 sentences, at most 700 characters>
<<<NOTE>>>
<the note body>

META. title: 4-8 words naming the question, no trailing period. topics: 1-5 lowercase kebab-case subject
tags. confidence: how well the evidence supports the answer. open: 0-3 unresolved questions worth
revisiting.

BRIEF. Lead with the answer. Plain, direct, no greeting, no restating the question, no "sure"/"great
question", no lists, no headings, no links. Include the numbers and the one caveat that decides how the
answer should be read.

NOTE. The durable record.
- Never restate the question; the host prints it above the body.
- First sentence answers. Then the mechanism, evidence or reasoning that makes it true, in the order a
  reader needs it. No preamble, no "in this note", no roadmap.
- Length follows the question. A fact gets two sentences; a mechanism gets its reasoning chain. Never pad
  to look thorough. Ceiling 700 words unless the question explicitly asks for depth.
- Structure with Obsidian callouts, not headings. `> [!abstract]` for the bottom line when the body runs
  past about 250 words. `> [!important]` for the decisive fact or condition. `> [!note]` for supporting
  detail. `> [!example]` for a worked example with units and intermediate steps. `> [!warning]` for
  limits, counterevidence, contested claims, or evidence you could not get. `> [!quote]` for a verbatim
  source quote, with its source link on the following line. At most four callouts; each must carry
  something prose would bury. Leave a blank `>` line inside a callout before a new paragraph.
- Other structure only when it beats prose: a Markdown table when three or more items are compared
  across two or more dimensions; a ```mermaid block for a mechanism, timeline, hierarchy, or decision
  flow; a numbered list for a procedure. Mermaid: at most 12 nodes, quoted labels, no styling
  directives, never `xychart-beta`.
- Math: `$...$` inline and `$$...$$` display. Never `\(` or `\[`.
- Headings inside the body: `###` at most twice.
- Every factual claim taken from the research packets carries that packet's source link verbatim,
  beside the claim. Never invent a link and never cite a source you were not given. Write from the
  conversation and general knowledge when there are no packets, and say so when that is the basis.
- Keep observation, evidence, inference and assumption distinct. Never present correlation as cause.
  Keep the quantities, dates and uncertainty the sources give; never invent precision.
- No filler: no praise, no "it's worth noting", no "in conclusion", no closing summary that repeats the
  answer, no offers to continue, no apologies, no emoji, no horizontal rules, no exclamation marks, no
  second-person coaching. Warmth is not information.
```

  Context sections appended, in this order, omitting empty ones: `## Question` (verbatim), `## Conversation so far` (last 3 exchanges, ≤6000 chars), `## Research packets` (JSON, ≤24000 chars, each finding carrying `claim`/`quote`/`ref`), `## Attachments` (extracted text ≤12000 chars; images as content blocks), `## User writing preferences` (`Style/Voice.md`, ≤4000 chars).
- `writerContext({question, recent, packets, attachmentText, voice}) -> {systemPrompt, userContent}`; `WriterOutcome = {meta, brief, note: string}`.
- `parseOutcome(text) -> {outcome, error?}` — split on the three markers; validate `META` as JSON with `title` string, `topics` array of ≤5 kebab-case strings, `confidence` in `high|medium|low`, `open` array of ≤3 strings; `BRIEF` non-empty; `NOTE` non-empty. Any violation → `error`.
- `writeAnswer({model, registry, thinkingLevel, …}) -> {outcome, usage}` — one `streamSimple` call (`MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS = 12000`, 180 s timeout, 90 s stall watchdog, images only when `model.input.includes('image')`). On `parseOutcome` error: one repair call appending `'Return the three sections again, in the required format, with no other text.'`; on a second failure use the deterministic fallback — `note` = the raw response with any markers stripped, `brief` = the first 700 characters up to the first sentence boundary, `meta = {title: sanitizeTitle(question), topics: [], confidence: 'low', open: []}` — and report `'Answer format was malformed; the note was saved without structure.'` as a warning. A turn never fails on formatting.

### Step 4 — Land the chat orchestration

New file: `src/chat.mjs` — `class Chat` and `class ChatSession` (the turn state machine). No SDK session, no `createAgentSession`, no session JSONL, no compaction hook, no publication staging.

`ChatSession` methods and exact sequence for `runTurn({text, images, ctx})`:

1. Refuse when a turn is in flight (`'Still working. Your draft is preserved; /discover stop interrupts.'` — reuse today's string).
2. `vault.ensure()`, `vault.acquireLock()`; resolve the chat: active chat from `_discover/active.json` when one exists and its note file is present, otherwise create one (id `randomUUID()`, title from the first turn's `META.title`, note path `Chats/<YYYY-MM-DD> <sanitizeTitle(title)>.md`, unique on collision).
3. `recent = recentExchanges(noteText, 3, 6000)`.
4. Stage attachments: staged PDFs are extracted now (`src/pdf.mjs`, text of pages 1–20 in `## Page <n>` sections, hashed into `_discover/pdf/<sha48>/`; page images only for up to two page numbers named in the question text when the model accepts images); images from `input.images` pass through as content blocks.
5. `route(...)` → progress `routing`.
6. When `research`, `runCrew(...)` → progress `researching <done>/<total>` with one widget line per query.
7. `writeAnswer(...)` → progress `writing`.
8. `normalizeObsidianMarkdown(note)` then `checkCitations(note, allowedRefs)`; unresolved refs are reported as a `> [!warning]- <n> citation(s) could not be resolved` callout appended to the section, listing them.
9. Assemble the section (heading, provenance callout, body, warnings), append to the note, recompute the related block in place, `upsertIndexChat`, `upsertIndexSource` for each fetched source, `noteSourceReference` for each cited source, `setActive`, `saveChat` (turns+1), `releaseLock()`.
10. `pi.sendMessage({customType:'discover', content: outcome.brief, display:true}, {triggerTurn:false})`.
11. Clear staged attachments on success; keep them on failure.

Turn caps: ≤4 workers, ≤4+1 model calls per worker, writer ≤2 calls, total ≤8 model calls; wall clock 5 minutes (`/discover stop` aborts the shared `AbortController`). A turn that fails before writing leaves the note untouched and restores the draft (`ctx.ui.setEditorText`) when the editor is empty, matching today's behavior. Cancelled or failed turns write nothing.

Progress/telemetry: status key `discover` with `discover · routing`, `discover · researching 2/3 · 12s`, `discover · writing`, `discover · saving note`, cleared on completion; a widget keyed `discover` renders one line per worker (`<query> — searching|reading|done (3 findings)|failed`) using the `setWidget(key, (tui, theme) => ({render, invalidate}))` + `tui.requestRender()` pattern copied from `scholar/loading-progress.ts:66-78`; the final status line `discover · 3 sources · 41s · 9.4k tok` stays until the next turn.

Rewrite `src/extension.mjs` and `src/commands.mjs`; add `src/progress.mjs`.

## Critical files & anchors

- `src/notes.mjs` — every literal the notes are made of (frontmatter keys, callout kinds, markers, titles). Implementer writes this first; the writer prompt and the note tests both depend on it.

## Context

`pi-discover` is a Pi extension (`pi install git:github.com/BasamAhmed640/pi-discover`, currently v0.6.3) that answers questions in the Pi composer and writes results into a linked Obsidian vault. Its current shape is the problem: two effort modes (`ask`/`deep`), a scripted evidence reviewer, an installed Obsidian companion plugin that renders answers as sandboxed-HTML chart iframes and `.html` "Reports", a browser-rendered layout checker, conversation forking, 11 model tools, and ~4.5 kLOC of source plus a committed plugin bundle.

The overhaul replaces that product shape: `/discover` becomes a chat — you type a question, the extension runs a small parallel research crew itself, streams back a short direct answer in the terminal, and appends a dense, information-heavy section to one Markdown note per chat in the vault. No modes, no plugin, no HTML, no layout checking, no forking. Vault linking and reconnect-to-a-linked-vault are kept exactly as they work today. Sources become real notes in the vault and are cited by wiki-link. Answers are concise and unsentimental: information first, no assistant warmth.

Decisions already fixed by the user: short brief in Pi + dense note in Obsidian; one running note per chat; adaptive agent fan-out; keep chats + images + PDFs (drop forking); related-chat links now via a cheap incremental index.

content.text:
[local://discover-overhaul-plan.md]
1:# Discover overhaul — chat answers that become Obsidian notes

316:## Assumptions & contingencies

318:- `@earendil-works/pi-ai` and `@earendil-works/pi-tui` resolve from an extension at runtime (true for `scholar` on this machine at SDK 0.85.1). If a runtime import fails, drop explicit thinking-level control and use `modelRegistry.complete(model, context, {signal, maxTokens, sessionId, transport:'sse', maxRetries:0})`, and render progress with `ctx.ui.setStatus` only.

320:- The keyless DuckDuckGo/Bing search path may rate-limit or challenge; that is already reported as a gap in the worker packet, and a worker that cannot retrieve anything produces an answer marked with the `> [!warning]` evidence limit rather than a silent claim.
321:- The user's existing vault pointer at `~/.pi/agent/research/config.json` and `_Research/vault.json` must keep working without relinking; if the implementer finds either file unreadable in the test vault, link it explicitly with `/discover vault` and record the failure in the final report instead of guessing at a new format.

# Discover overhaul — chat answers that become Obsidian notes

## Context

`pi-discover` is a Pi extension (`pi install git:github.com/BasamAhmed640/pi-discover`, currently v0.6.3) that answers questions in the Pi composer and writes results into a linked Obsidian vault. Its current shape is the problem: two effort modes (`ask`/`deep`), a scripted evidence reviewer, an installed Obsidian companion plugin that renders answers as sandboxed-HTML chart iframes and `.html` "Reports", a browser-rendered layout checker, conversation forking, 11 model tools, and ~4.5 kLOC of source plus a committed plugin bundle.

The overhaul replaces that product shape: `/discover` becomes a chat — you type a question, the extension runs a small parallel research crew itself, streams back a short direct answer in the terminal, and appends a dense, information-heavy section to one Markdown note per chat in the vault. No modes, no plugin, no HTML, no layout checking, no forking. Vault linking and reconnect-to-a-linked-vault are kept exactly as they work today. Sources become real notes in the vault and are cited by wiki-link. Answers are concise and unsentimental: information first, no assistant warmth.

Decisions already fixed by the user: short brief in Pi + dense note in Obsidian; one running note per chat; adaptive agent fan-out; keep chats + images + PDFs (drop forking); related-chat links now via a cheap incremental index.

## Verified facts this plan relies on

Run of `main` @ `8195ae8a` fetched read-only into session scratch (`local://pi-discover-src/`); Pi SDK/SDK docs read from the installed `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@0.85.1`.

- Extension contract: `ExtensionAPI` gives `registerCommand`, `registerTool`, `on('input'|'session_start'|'session_shutdown'|…)`, `sendMessage({customType, content, display}, {triggerTurn})`, `appendEntry`, `registerMessageRenderer`, `setActiveTools`; `ExtensionContext` gives `ui` (`setStatus`, `setWidget`, `setEditorComponent`, `select`, `confirm`, `input`, `notify`, `getEditorText`, `setEditorText`), `model`, `thinkingLevel`, `modelRegistry`, `sessionManager`, `hasUI`, `isIdle()`.
- `ModelRegistry.complete(model, context, options)` and `ModelRuntime`'s `streamSimple(model, context, options)` take a plain `{systemPrompt, messages, tools}` context — stateless single-shot calls, no session required. A working precedent exists on this machine: `C:\Users\basam\.pi\agent\extensions\scholar\review-runtime.ts` runs a bounded tool loop with `modelRegistry.getProvider()` + `getApiKeyAndHeaders()` + `provider.streamSimple(..., {reasoning, signal, maxTokens, sessionId, transport:'sse', maxRetries:0})`, and `review-layer.ts` fans 12 of those out concurrently. `clampThinkingLevel` is imported from `@earendil-works/pi-ai`; `@earendil-works/pi-tui` is importable for widget components. Neither is declared as a dependency in that extension's `package.json`.
- `InputEvent` carries `text` and `images?: ImageContent[]` — pasted images arrive with the submitted message, no attach command needed for images.
- A message sent with `pi.sendMessage({customType, content, display:true})` is rendered by the host as a labeled box containing **Markdown** (`dist/modes/interactive/components/custom-message.js`: `new Markdown(text, 0, 0, markdownTheme, …)`); a custom renderer is optional.
- Current vault writes (to be replaced): `Conversations/`, `Sources/<uuid>/`, `Knowledge/`, `Visuals/<uuid>/`, `Attachments/`, `_Research/*`, and `.obsidian/plugins/pi-research/`. Machine-local vault pointer: `~/.pi/agent/research/config.json` = `{version:1, vaultRoot, vaultId}` (env override `PI_RESEARCH_CONFIG_DIR`); vault identity today at `<vault>/_Research/vault.json`.
- Dev loop command: `pi -e ./index.ts` (`docs/extensions.md:103-106`). Install/update: `pi install git:…`, `pi update git:…`.

---

## Approach

Ordered so the tree stays valid after each step: new modules land first (unreferenced), then the host surface switches to them, then the obsolete surface is deleted, then tests/docs.

### Step 1 — Land the new vault layer

New files: `src/vault.mjs`, `src/index-store.mjs`, `src/notes.mjs`.

**Folder and file contract** (all under the linked vault root; `_` prefix marks machine-owned dirs):

```text
_discover/vault.json         {"version":1,"id":<uuid>,"createdAt":<iso>}
_discover/active.json        {"version":1,"chatId":<uuid>}
_discover/writer.lock        {"version":1,"pid":<n>,"host":"<os.hostname()>","startedAt":<iso>,"token":<uuid>}
_discover/index.json         {"version":1,"updatedAt":<iso>,
                              "chats":{"<chatId>":{"path","title","topics":[],"sources":[<sourceId>],"updatedAt"}},
                              "sources":{"<sourceId>":{"path","url","title","kind":"web|pdf","hash","retrievedAt"}}}
_discover/chats/<chatId>.json {"version":1,"id","title","notePath","createdAt","updatedAt","model","topics":[],"sources":[],"turns":<n>}
_discover/pdf/<sha48>/…      extracted page text + page PNG cache (kept from current pdf.mjs)
Chats/<YYYY-MM-DD> <Title>.md
Sources/<Title> (<hash8>).md
Style/Voice.md               read-only, user-owned, optional, ≤4000 chars injected into the writer prompt
```

`src/notes.mjs` exports pure builders/parsers (no fs):

- `frontmatter(fields) -> string` — YAML block, keys in fixed order.
- `callout(kind, title, bodyLines, {collapsed}) -> string` — `> [!kind]- Title` + `> ` lines; emits `>` for blank lines inside the callout.
- `questionHeading(index, text) -> string` — `## <n>. <text>` (question verbatim, single line; newlines collapsed to spaces).
- `appendExchange(noteText, exchange) -> string` — appends `\n\n` + heading + provenance callout + body section before the trailing related-marker block when present, otherwise at end.
- `relatedBlock(entries) -> string` — wrapped in `<!-- discover:related:start -->` / `<!-- discover:related:end -->`.
- `rewriteBlock(noteText, marker, block) -> string` — replace between markers; missing markers → append at end.
- `splitExchanges(noteText) -> [{question, body}]` — split on `^## ` headings.
- `recentExchanges(noteText, count, charBudget) -> string` — last N exchanges, trimmed to the last `charBudget` characters on whole lines.
- `normalizeObsidianMarkdown(text) -> string` — outside fenced code blocks convert `\(…\)` → `$…$` and `\[…\]` → `$$…$$`; collapse 3+ blank lines to 2; strip trailing whitespace; guarantee a trailing newline.
- `sanitizeTitle(text) -> string` — strip `[\\/:*?"<>|#^\[\]]`, collapse whitespace, trim trailing dots/spaces, cap 80 chars, empty → `Untitled chat`.
- `sourceFileName(title, hash8) -> string`, `chatFileName(date, title) -> string`, `sourceRef(sourceId, title, hash8) -> "[[Sources/<Title> (<hash8>)|<Title>]]"` — the exact wiki-link string handed to the model.
- `uniquePath(exists, dir, baseName, ext) -> string` — appends ` 2`, ` 3`… on collision.

`src/vault.mjs` exports `openVault(root, {scholarRoots}) -> Vault` and class `Vault`:

- `ensure()` — create `_discover/`, `_discover/chats/`, `Chats/`, `Sources/`; write `_discover/vault.json` when absent, adopting the id from `_Research/vault.json` when that legacy file exists and parses (keeps an existing linked vault's identity stable). Identity mismatch against the stored pointer throws `'Discover vault identity does not match the saved binding'`.
- `acquireLock()` / `releaseLock()` / `unlockStale()` — token/pid/host lock. Stale when `host === os.hostname()` and the pid is not alive → steal silently; a live lock from another host throws `'This vault is being written by <host>. Close that Pi instance or run /discover unlock.'`.
- `writeFile(relPath, text)` / `readFile(relPath)` — atomic temp-file + rename, `mkdir -p`, per-path promise serialization, path-escape and symlink guard (copy the guard rules from the current `src/vault.mjs:safePath`).
- `storeSource({url, title, kind, text, hash}) -> {id, path, ref, title, reused}` — dedupe key `sha256(normalizedUrl)` for `web` (lowercase scheme+host, no fragment, drop `utm_*`/`fbclid`/`gclid`/`ref`, remaining query params sorted) and `sha256(fileBytes)` for `pdf`; reuse the existing `Sources/<Title> (<hash8>).md` when the id is already indexed by recording a new reference entry, else write it (template below).
- `noteSourceReference(sourceId, chatPath)` — rewrite the source note's `## Referenced by` block between `<!-- discover:refs:start -->`/`:end -->` with `- [[<chat note>]]` lines, deduped, sorted.
- `relatedChats(chatId, {limit:3})` — from the index: other chats with `sharedSources >= 2 || sharedTopics >= 3`, ties broken by most recent `updatedAt`.
- `upsertIndexChat(record)` / `upsertIndexSource(record)` / `setActive(chatId)` / `getActive()` / `getChat(id)` / `listChats()` / `saveChat(record)`.

**Chat note template** (`Chats/<date> <Title>.md`):

```markdown
---
discover: chat
chat: <chatId>
title: <title>
created: <iso>
updated: <iso>
topics: [a, b]
tags: [discover/a, discover/b]
sources: 3
model: <provider/model-id>
---

# <title>

## 1. <question 1 verbatim>

> [!info]- Asked 2026-09-17 09:12 · 3 sources · <provider/model-id>
> [[Sources/AlphaEvolve (1b5c7b49)|AlphaEvolve]] · [[Sources/…]]

<note body>

<!-- discover:related:start -->
> [!link]- Related
> - [[Chats/2026-09-14 …]] — shares [[Sources/…]]
<!-- discover:related:end -->
```

# Discover overhaul — chat answers that become Obsidian notes

## Context

`pi-discover` is a Pi extension (`pi install git:github.com/BasamAhmed640/pi-discover`, currently v0.6.3) that answers questions in the Pi composer and writes results into a linked Obsidian vault. Its current shape is the problem: two effort modes (`ask`/`deep`), a scripted evidence reviewer, an installed Obsidian companion plugin that renders answers as sandboxed-HTML chart iframes and `.html` "Reports", a browser-rendered layout checker, conversation forking, 11 model tools, and ~4.5 kLOC of source plus a committed plugin bundle.

The overhaul replaces that product shape: `/discover` becomes a chat — you type a question, the extension runs a small parallel research crew itself, streams back a short direct answer in the terminal, and appends a dense, information-heavy section to one Markdown note per chat in the vault. No modes, no plugin, no HTML, no layout checking, no forking. Vault linking and reconnect-to-a-linked-vault are kept exactly as they work today. Sources become real notes in the vault and are cited by wiki-link. Answers are concise and unsentimental: information first, no assistant warmth.

Decisions already fixed by the user: short brief in Pi + dense note in Obsidian; one running note per chat; adaptive agent fan-out; keep chats + images + PDFs (drop forking); related-chat links now via a cheap incremental index.
